the determinants of government turnover are complex and multifaceted, but the evidence suggests that pay reform can be an effective tool in retaining employees.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the IRS has been able to increase the accountability of its supervisors while maintaining their morale.
the effects of accountability on turnover intention are more complicated than is often suggested, and that pay incentives may not have a uniform effect on turnover.
the effects of performance-based pay are not uniform, but depend on the context in which it is implemented and the characteristics of the employees.
The main takeaway from our work is that
turnover intentions in the public sector are not solely a function of compensation.
turnover intention is not simply a function of pay and performance, but is also a function of the social and organizational environment.

turnover intention in government is a complex function of the institutional environment, individual characteristics, and preferences, and that pay reforms can be an effective tool to reduce turnover among government employees.
